# Datasheet — Synthetic Submittal Corpus

**Status: SYNTHETIC.** Every document under `data/corpus/synthetic/` was generated by this
project from a committed seed and the E001 project/vendor roster. No document is a real
submittal, no vendor is a real firm, no project is a real project, and nothing here was
derived from proprietary, confidential, or customer material.

This datasheet accompanies the synthetic layer and is required to sit beside it (FR-027). It
lives at `data/corpus/synthetic/datasheet.md`, outside every corpus location, so it is not
itself a corpus document requiring a manifest entry (VR-055).

**No digest value is reproduced in this document.** A digest copied into prose is a second
source of truth that nothing updates, and a stale one here would be indistinguishable from
real drift. The manifests record every digest; this datasheet describes what they cover
(VR-054).

## Motivation

The synthetic layer exists because the two things this project must demonstrate — extraction
from construction submittals and a submittal-log forecast — need submittal documents, and no
corpus of real ones can be shipped. Real submittals are contractor and government working
papers: they are not public domain, they carry firm names and contract detail, and vendoring
them would break the provenance claim the whole repository rests on.

Generating them instead makes three properties available that a scraped corpus could not
offer. The ground truth is known by construction, so extraction accuracy is measurable rather
than estimated. The population is fixed and small enough to read in full during review. And
the documents can be made deliberately, recordedly messy, so downstream results stay
partitionable by the irregularity that caused them rather than pooled into one number.

The layer is paired with a vendored public-domain specification layer under
`data/corpus/real/`. That pairing is the point: a synthetic submittal references a real
specification section, so the specification-to-submittal join every later epic needs has both
sides.

## Composition

| Population | Count | Source of the identity |
|---|---|---|
| Corpus locations | 5 | One per roster project, `data/corpus/synthetic/PRJ-00N/` |
| Projects | 5 | E001 roster, via `read_roster()` — this epic declares none |
| Vendors | 12 | E001 roster, via `read_roster()` — this epic declares none |
| Documents | 25 or more | Generated, one PDF per submittal transmittal |
| Pages per document | 2 | Transmittal block, then the submitted-item list |

Each document is a submittal transmittal record carrying six structural fields: a transmittal
number, the referenced specification section, a submittal descriptor code, an
approving-authority marker, a revision suffix, and a reviewer action stamp. Every project
carries at least one resubmittal chain — two documents sharing a submittal number with an
incremented revision suffix and a different action code.

Material items on a transmittal name an equipment category drawn from the committed
`equipment-category-map.json`. Every category in that map resolves to a MasterFormat section
the vendored real layer actually holds, so no item points at a specification the corpus does
not carry.

Irregularities are recorded per document as a closed five-value set:
`INCONSISTENT_FIELD_LABEL`, `MISSING_OR_BLANK_FIELD`, `OUT_OF_ORDER_DATE`, `PAGE_SPLIT_FIELD`,
and `SCAN_DEGRADATION`. The first four are structural and are re-derived from the emitted PDF
by validation, independently of what the generator recorded. The fifth is not derivable from
structure and is evidenced by the injector's own unit tests instead.

No personal data appears anywhere in the layer. There are no names of individuals, no contact
details, no addresses, and no attribution to any identifiable person or organization.

## Generation Process

Generation is offline, seeded, and model-free. The generator reads the roster through E001's
single reader, the committed `generation-config.json`, `equipment-category-map.json`, and
`field-label-vocabulary.json`, and nothing else. It reaches no network and invokes no language
model; that is enforced by an import contract over the module graph and by a socket guard
installed before the generator package is imported, not merely asserted here.

Nothing in the pipeline reads a clock. Every date on every document is derived by arithmetic
from the committed `generation_date` constant, and the renderer is opened with ReportLab's
`invariant` flag so the creation timestamp and the file identifier are content-derived rather
than clock-derived. A re-run under an unchanged seed and roster therefore rewrites no byte.

Reproducibility is recorded rather than claimed. Each entry carries a `document_model_hash`
over the pre-render document model, a `roster_hash` carrying the reader's canonical-content
digest of the roster, and a `generation_inputs` mapping of raw-byte digests over the three
committed generation inputs. Re-running the generator reproduces every model hash; editing the
roster or any generation input moves a recorded value and fails validation, naming every
document generated from it.

Degraded pages are constructed rather than scanned: the body region is rasterized and the same
text is re-laid beneath it in an invisible render mode, while the citation anchor — the
document identifier and page number — is drawn in a header band the raster never covers.

## Preprocessing

**None. No source dataset was cleaned, filtered, labelled, or sampled**, because there is no
source dataset. Every document in this layer was synthesized from the roster, the committed
generation inputs, and the seed; nothing was collected, scraped, de-duplicated, balanced,
truncated, or otherwise conditioned before use.

This section is present and non-empty deliberately even though its answer is "none". An
omitted preprocessing section reads as an oversight, and a reader cannot tell an unanswered
question from one whose answer happens to be nothing. The irregularity injection described
above is emphatically not preprocessing: it is part of generation, applied to documents this
project created, and it is recorded per document rather than applied silently.

## Intended Uses

Intended use is demonstration and evaluation of the procurement-risk pipeline: document
ingestion, field extraction with page citations, cross-document identity resolution, and the
submittal-log forecast that consumes the resulting records.

Appropriate uses:

- Measuring extraction precision and recall against a known ground truth.
- Exercising retrieval and ranking over a mixed specification-and-submittal corpus.
- Partitioning downstream results by recorded irregularity class.

Uses this corpus does not support:

- Any claim about real federal submittal practice, transmittal vocabularies, or form layout.
  The codes and labels are an approximation, disclosed under `Stated Limits`.
- Any claim about robustness to genuine scanning or recognition error. See `Stated Limits`.
- Training or evaluating a model intended for production use on real submittals without an
  independent evaluation on real documents.
- Any statement about real firms, projects, or places. None appears here.

## Distribution

The layer is committed to this repository and travels with it. A clone that has never run the
generator holds the complete corpus; nothing is fetched or generated on checkout.

There are no distribution restrictions. The license basis recorded on every entry is
`project-generated-no-third-party-rights`: the documents were generated by this project, no
third-party material is reproduced, and no third-party rights attach. No copyrighted reference
standard is reproduced anywhere in the layer — where such a standard is relevant it is cited
by number and not included.

The layer is deliberately shipped as plain committed files rather than through large-file
indirection, so an evaluator reading the repository sees the same bytes validation reads.

## Maintenance

The synthetic layer is a generated artifact, not an editable record. A document or a manifest
edited by hand fails validation on the next run, because every `content_hash` is recomputed
from the file's bytes and every manifest is byte-compared against what the writer emits.

Three changes require regeneration, and validation names each of them:

- The roster's content changes. Every entry's `roster_hash` goes stale and every document is
  named; regeneration or reverting the roster are the only resolutions.
- A generation input changes — the generation config, the equipment-category map, or the
  field-label vocabulary. The recorded `generation_inputs` digest for that input no longer
  matches its bytes, and every document whose own entry records it is named.
- The pinned renderer version changes. This is reported as a regeneration event with both
  versions named rather than as a validation failure: the document-model hashes and the
  manifest set do not move, so only the rendered PDFs are re-emitted.

The corpus is frozen for the ingestion window of the epic that consumes it. That freeze is a
convention no check observes — the drift rules above are after-the-fact detectors, not
preventers, and they are stated as such rather than presented as enforcement.

## Stated Limits

**The transmittal codes and field labels are a documented approximation of federal submittal
practice, and this corpus is not a reproduction of any live form.** The current revision of
the government transmittal form returned HTTP 403 to automated retrieval, so its descriptor
series, reviewer action letters, and field labels could not be verified against the source. An
unverified vocabulary presented as the authentic one would be a provenance claim this project
cannot support. The codes are shaped to be plausible so downstream extraction exercises the
same structure; nothing downstream may claim this corpus evidences the real form's vocabulary,
and any result measured over it is a result about an approximation.

**The retained text layer carries no recognition error, so this corpus evidences no robustness
to genuine scan noise.** Degraded pages are built by rasterizing a rendered page and re-laying
the *same* text beneath the image invisibly. The visual body therefore looks scanned while the
extracted characters remain exactly what the generator wrote — zero character error, zero
transposition, zero dropped word. Real scanned submittals passed through optical character
recognition carry all three. Extraction accuracy measured here is an upper bound that a real
scanned corpus would not reproduce, and reading it as evidence of recognition robustness is
the specific misreading this disclosure exists to prevent.

Further limits, stated rather than left to be discovered:

- The population is small and uniform in kind: one document type, two pages each, from one
  generator. It exercises structure, not the diversity of a real project archive.
- Layout variety comes from a fixed set of per-vendor templates. Two documents from one vendor
  differ in content, not in layout.
- That any *particular* document is visually degraded is generator-asserted. Validation
  establishes only the necessary condition that a document recording `SCAN_DEGRADATION` carries
  a page-sized raster — at least half the page, which is as strong as this condition can be
  made, because the citation anchor is required to sit outside every raster and a literally
  full-page image is therefore forbidden by construction. The injector's unit tests, whose
  oracle is the same page rendered with the profile disabled, are the evidence that
  degradation occurred.
- The raster is a re-rendering of the page's own text at a fixed sampling resolution, not a
  photograph of paper. It carries no page skew from a feeder, no binding shadow, no dust, and
  no ink bleed; blur, contrast loss, speckle, and a small rotation are the only artefacts, and
  each is bounded by the committed generation configuration.
- The irregularity injector and the structural deriver both read the same committed
  field-label vocabulary. A mistake common to both would make the re-derivation agree for the
  wrong reason; hand-authored fixtures stand in for a second vocabulary, but nothing
  re-derives the vocabulary itself.
- Dates, quantities, and lead times on these documents are drawn from the seed. They are
  plausible in shape and carry no empirical distribution behind them.
